limitations: The directory renders whatever GET /api/v1/connectors/catalog returns; it was exercised against the loopback double of that route table, not against the server implementation.
workItems.notes: Rows come only from the server catalogue. Search and facets (service, ecosystem, custody, capability dimension, runtime, evidence, support level) run over the whole inventory; paging is a rendering budget ('Show N more') and never a filter, asserted with a row 26 pages deep. Alternatives share a group heading and stay separate cards with their own support badge, custody badges, evidence chip and configuration readiness. Deep links preserved: / opens the directory, ?connector= opens the drawer, ?connection= resumes, mode/section are kept when the query is rewritten. StatusChip and HandoffMeter are reused from src/react/connectors.tsx.

limitations: Publish/activate is a 'propose a runtime binding' call to POST /bindings; whatever richer activation the server ends up offering is not yet surfaced.
The viewer field it reads is a proposal (see contractChanges); with nothing reported, operator controls stay hidden.
workItems.notes: Import review shows provenance (format and version, origin, capture time, exact-byte digest, normalized digest, native identity and version, importer, licence, overlays), diagnostics grouped by category with blocking first, the per-dimension mapping table, proposed authentication profiles with their declared endpoints and scopes, declared servers marked declared-not-approved, and runtime configuration requirements. Only issue codes, pointers and the importer's sanitized messages are rendered: a canary key in an uploaded document never reaches the review region. Binding stays disabled while a blocking issue stands.

limitations: Dynamic options are fetched by invoking the operation the field names; a server that describes dynamic fields some other way is not covered.
POST /connections/:ref/collect is a proposed route (see contractChanges); without it a secret field cannot be submitted.
workItems.notes: Non-secret values live in component state; a field the server classifies as secret is never mirrored into state, a draft, the URL or a log. It is read from the form once on submit, sent to the private collector, and replaced by the returned reference before the handoff input is posted — asserted with a canary that appears in exactly one request body. Dynamic fields render dependsOn-driven selects with their own loading, blocked and error states, fetched through an invoke of the named operation with the dependency values.

limitations: Organization ownership is offered only when the catalogue's viewer reports that owner kind; until the server reports it, the control is permanently disabled and says so.
workItems.notes: Every PR #39 drawer control was audited against the route table and the audit table is in docs/connector-directory.md. Kept and mapped: auth family to intent.profileId, environment to bindingRef (approved bindings only), target to intent.target, identity preference to ownerKind, interruption budget to intent.interruption. Removed: managed/custom endpoint declaration, per-family endpoint and environment-name fields, shared/per-user key mode, every capability toggle, the verification off-switch and the expiry select. Capability toggles became a read-only CapabilityStatus report; a unit test asserts no control inside it and no control label mentioning verification or key sharing.

limitations: Target options are offered by the server as handoff fields once a flow is under way; before connecting, the target is typed and the copy says the server must observe it.
workItems.notes: The connection reports claim kinds, observation time, validity (including 'the provider stated no expiry'), limitations and the exact verified target, plus the custody badge, evidence freshness and a handoff meter counting distinct handoffs. Reconnect requires ticking an explicit account-change intent and sends expectedRevision; a stale revision is refused. Disconnect asks for a scope, explains all three in their own words, and renders the DisconnectResult per scope with the sharedWith impact list. Indeterminate outcomes are named as unknown and reconciling. A closed popup, a postMessage and the 'I finished' button only trigger a poll.

limitations: Axe covers the directory and drawer of the harness page; the reference application's own shell is audited by its existing specs.
workItems.notes: Focus enters the drawer, Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside it, Escape closes it and focus returns to the card — verified in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Field labels carry the field name only; hints, loading and error states are separate aria-describedby elements. The handoff window is opened on the click and navigated when the server answers; a blocked window falls back to same-window navigation and the callback returns to the connection, which is re-read from the server. Offline disables connecting and invoking and says nothing is queued; 401 clears the surface and asks for sign-in. The service worker is untouched and a test asserts it never names a connector route or /api/, and that the client always sends cache: no-store. No WebMCP dependency exists in these surfaces.

limitations: scripts/check-bundle.mjs enforces a total-download ceiling across every chunk, so mounting these surfaces in the reference application fails it even though the reference page itself grows by 0.77 kB raw / 0.30 kB gzip. The ceiling needs a deliberate raise (see integrationPatches); I did not change the script.
Splitting the connection surface into its own chunk was tried and reverted: Rollup keeps it in the same chunk as the directory, so it bought nothing.
workItems.notes: The components take a host-supplied client (any transport implementing the typed interface) and host-supplied window management, so a host embedding them from @ceremony/auth/react supplies both. Browser tests run against a harness that esbuild-bundles the shipped components and serves them, the route table and a fixture provider from an ephemeral loopback port, with a second origin for the untrusted-message case; no dev server and no fixed port. Screenshots are written only to testInfo.outputPath from fixture data.

contractChanges.change: src/core/connectors/client.ts adds a browser client with no changes to existing contracts.
contractChanges.compatibility: Additive module. Nothing existing imports it yet.

contractChanges.change: Proposed additive field on GET /api/v1/connectors/catalog: `viewer: { capabilities: string[], ownerKinds: OwnerKind[] }`, equivalently the headers `x-ceremony-capabilities` and `x-ceremony-owner-kinds` (the client reads either).
contractChanges.compatibility: Optional. Absent, the client defaults to { capabilities: [], ownerKinds: ['user'] }: operator controls stay hidden and organization ownership stays disabled with 'requires administrator policy'. This mirrors the existing /api/v1/teaching/capabilities pattern.

contractChanges.change: Proposed additive field on the human connection projection's `presentation`: `fields?: FieldDescriptor[]`, where a descriptor is { name, label, type, required, classification, description?, options?, dynamic?: { operationRef, dependsOn[] } }.
contractChanges.compatibility: Optional; only an in-app handoff carries it. Without it the drawer renders the url/userCode/instructions it already renders. It is how a server asks for input in the app (MCP input_required, Microsoft dynamic fields) without the browser inventing a form.

contractChanges.change: Proposed additive route: POST /api/v1/connectors/connections/:ref/collect { values } -> { secretRef }, the connector equivalent of the existing /collect on ceremonies.
contractChanges.compatibility: Additive. Required before a secret-classified handoff field can be submitted; the UI sends only the returned reference to /handoffs/:ref/input.

contractChanges.change: Observed: POST /bindings returns either the binding or { binding }. The client accepts both.
contractChanges.compatibility: No server change needed; noted so the shape can be settled.

The budget is a total-download ceiling across every chunk, so the new on-demand chunks fail it even though the reference page is unchanged. Measured with the mount patch above: index 471.53 kB raw / 145.87 kB gzip (from 470.76 / 145.57), connectors chunk 66.46 kB raw / 20.75 kB gzip, connector-review chunk 12.13 kB raw / 3.93 kB gzip, totals 570986 raw / 178663 gzip against a budget of 495000 / 154000. Either raise the ceiling deliberately (suggest 580000 raw / 182000 gzip, with the reason written beside the previous raise) or leave these surfaces out of the reference build.
